overview: Two Gram-negative diplococci in the same genus that share morphology and growth requirements but cause very different diseases.
genZNote: Same genus, very different Tinder profile — one's an STI, the other crashes your meninges.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: A Gram-negative diplococcus causing the sexually transmitted infection gonorrhea.
aspects.valueB: A Gram-negative diplococcus that colonizes the nasopharynx and can cause invasive meningococcal disease.

aspects.label: Primary Disease
aspects.valueA: Gonorrhea — urethritis, cervicitis, pelvic inflammatory disease, and disseminated gonococcal infection.
aspects.valueB: Meningococcemia and meningitis, especially in adolescents and young adults, often with a petechial/purpuric rash.

aspects.label: Transmission
aspects.valueA: Sexual contact or perinatal transmission (ophthalmia neonatorum).
aspects.valueB: Respiratory droplets; carried asymptomatically in the nasopharynx of many healthy people.

aspects.label: Capsule
aspects.valueB: Polysaccharide capsule is a major virulence factor and the basis for serogroup vaccines (A, B, C, W, Y).

aspects.label: Culture Media
aspects.valueA: Grown on selective Thayer-Martin (chocolate agar with antibiotics) in a CO2-enriched atmosphere.
aspects.valueB: Also grows on chocolate agar/Thayer-Martin with CO2, but is not typically isolated from genital specimens.

aspects.label: Biochemical Characteristics
aspects.valueB: Oxidase-positive; ferments both glucose and maltose (a key differentiating test).

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueB: Respiratory transmission, encapsulated, ferments glucose and maltose.
